description: Use to re-plan with confirmed requirements (after recommend_stack) or with exact inputs. Reads only; no sign-in. Given confirmed requirements as capability ids, recommend a vendor per category with a runner-up, requirement fit, cost now, cost at forecast scale, year-one cost after perks, cost cliffs, trade-offs and blockers. Use recommend_stack instead when you only have a plain-language description. Example: {"mau_now":5000,"mau_forecast":20000,"profile_id":"booking_marketplace","requirements":[{"capability":"auth.google"},{"capability":"payments.merchant_of_record"}],"founder":{"gateways":["mercury"]}}. How to present the result: show the stack table (pick and runner-up per category, monthly cost now and at forecast) and the totals. For each price give its source's verified date, or say it is unverified seed data. Show every caveat word for word; never round, merge or drop one. Mention requirement gaps, blockers and trade-offs, and each pick's "weighed" note when a cheaper vendor lost on lock-in, setup work or seed prices. Offer the alternatives (cheapest, fewest vendors) with what each changes, its cost and its share_url. List not_planned as needed but not in the totals. Ask the questions (most expensive first) and re-plan with the answers in the argument each names (per_user, revenue_per_mau_usd, builder_profile); when the user says an assumption is right, add the question id to confirmed so it isn't asked again. On a saved stack, keep answers with update_saved_stack (answers). Link share_url so the user can open the full result on kongreviews.com. Do not add vendors or prices that are not in the result.

accounts.description: For a business product counted in customers ("50 clinics now, 500 next year"): customers now and at the forecast, and people using it at each (default 10). Users are worked out from these when mau_now is not given.

answers.description: Interview answers by question id, each an option id from compare_architectures, e.g. {"server":"dynamic","logins":"consumers","threat":"public","ops":"managed"}.

app_type.description: Kind of app, from Product Hunt's categories: productivity, engineering_development, design_creative, finance, marketing_sales, data_analysis, platforms, no_code, product_addons, llms, ai_agents, voice_ai, social_community, health_fitness, family, lifestyle, web3, ecommerce, travel, physical_products, booking_marketplace, content_site, ios_on_device. Sets the usage profile and, when users are not given, typical users at launch and after the forecast period.

architecture.description: Plan with only this architecture's vendors, from compare_architectures (e.g. serverless_nextjs, cloudflare_edge, vps_cloudflare).

build_tool.description: The build tool the user named, as a coding vendor id (lovable, bolt, replit, base44, v0, cursor, claude-code, github-copilot…): the plan uses it. An app builder that hosts the app and runs its database and sign-in (Lovable, Bolt, Replit, Base44) covers those, so they are not planned separately.

builder_profile.description: Who builds it. developer picks an AI coding agent, non_developer an app builder (and counts setup work double). Given without categories, the plan adds the build tool (coding).

chosen_vendors.description: A vendor chosen for a category, as category → vendor id (e.g. {"sms": "twilio"}): only that vendor is considered there, and the category is planned if it wasn't. Accepted changes (accept_change) are kept this way.

confirmed.description: Ids of questions whose assumption the user confirmed as right (e.g. ["region", "builder"]), so the plan stops asking them. A question answered with a figure goes in its own argument instead (per_user, revenue_per_mau_usd…).

founder.description: Optional company details used only to find startup perks.

existing_customer_of.description: Vendor ids you already pay (new-customer perks are excluded).

gateways.description: Perk gateways you belong to, e.g. ["mercury", "stripe_atlas", "yc"].

mau_now.description: Monthly active users now. Without it, a new product of the app type at launch.

needs.description: Needs the plan should list even though they are not priced (directory category ids such as maps, vector_db, speech), from recommend_stack's requirements_read.needs.

output_destination.description: Where the answer goes. chat (default): summary for the conversation. document: a section ready to paste into a PRD. code: adds npm packages and environment variable names for each pick.

per_1k_mau.description: Override usage per 1,000 MAU. Units: mau, seat, request_million, bandwidth_gb, db_storage_gb, egress_gb, email, event, error_event, compute_hour, revenue_usd, transaction, ai_input_ktok, ai_output_ktok, kv_read, kv_write, ci_hour, file_storage_gb, file_egress_gb, file_write, file_read, video_min_stored, video_min_delivered, sms, job_run, search_request, search_record.

per_user.description: Usage per active user a month, e.g. {"sms": 2, "file_storage_gb": 0.2, "ai_input_ktok": 30}. Replaces the profile and the filled-in defaults for those units; a plan's questions say which unit each answer sets. Units: mau, seat, request_million, bandwidth_gb, db_storage_gb, egress_gb, email, event, error_event, compute_hour, revenue_usd, transaction, ai_input_ktok, ai_output_ktok, kv_read, kv_write, ci_hour, file_storage_gb, file_egress_gb, file_write, file_read, video_min_stored, video_min_delivered, sms, job_run, search_request, search_record.

platforms.description: Where the app runs; with architecture, a phone-only app leaves out web hosting.

profile_id.description: Usage profile: b2b_saas (default), consumer_app, booking_marketplace, content_site, ios_on_device. Defaults to the app type's profile.

ranking.description: balanced (default): monthly cost plus a small monthly weight for lock-in, setup work before first use and unverified seed prices, so a slightly cheaper vendor that is hard to leave or slow to set up can lose. cost: price alone. simplest: fewest vendors and least setup (one vendor covering several categories wins unless the others are much cheaper). Each plan lists the other two as alternatives when their picks differ.

capability.description: Capability id from list_capabilities, e.g. auth.saml_sso.

source.description: The PRD sentence this came from.

revenue_per_mau_usd.description: Average monthly revenue per active user (for payment fees).

seats.description: Team members on per-seat plans. Default 1.

task_intent.description: What the user is trying to do, in a few words, e.g. "pick a stack for an MVP" or "cost section for an investor deck". No names or contact details.

transactions_per_mau.description: Payments per active user per month.

name: plan_stack

assumptions.description: Usage and pricing assumptions behind the numbers.

caveats.description: Show to the user word for word.

completeness.description: On plan and project results: complete, complete_with_assumptions, incomplete or needs_clarification, with the reasons. Say plainly when it is not complete.

data.description: The tool result. Its shape depends on the tool.

disclosures.description: Always includes the neutrality note: no vendor pays for a place in the answer. Link its url when you mention how Kong Reviews is paid.

project.description: On results about a saved project: its id and the context version the answer was computed on. Pass both back in follow-up calls.
